findings.title: Make `order()` a default method so existing providers keep compiling
Equal priorities make provider selection arbitrary, so a FIPS deployment can silently use non-FIPS crypto
Avoid passing a built string as the format argument to `debugf`
Remove the dead encoder calls and validate the input length in `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`

response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Maintainability
Title: Make `order()` a default method so existing providers keep compiling

Affected:
- common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java:39-44

Explanation:
`int order();` is added to a public SPI interface as an abstract method. Every `CryptoProvider` implementation outside these three modules will break:
- Third-party providers will fail to compile.
- Already-compiled providers will throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime when `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` calls `CryptoProvider::order` while sorting.

Other implementations may exist elsewhere in the repo (test modules, adapters). I cannot see them from this diff. A default implementation avoids the break for all of them.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
default int order() {
    return 0;
}
~~~

## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Security
Title: Equal priorities make provider selection arbitrary, so a FIPS deployment can silently use non-FIPS crypto

Affected:
- common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:57-71
- crypto/default/src/main/java/org/keycloak/crypto/def/DefaultCryptoProvider.java:82-85
- crypto/elytron/src/main/java/org/keycloak/crypto/elytron/WildFlyElytronProvider.java:75-78
- crypto/fips1402/src/main/java/org/keycloak/crypto/fips/FIPS1402Provider.java:113-116

Explanation:
Before this change, having more than one provider on the classpath raised an `IllegalStateException`. That error protected against misconfiguration.

Now the list is sorted by `order()`, but Default, Elytron and FIPS all return 200. Ties keep `ServiceLoader` order, which depends on classpath order. As a result:
- If both `keycloak-crypto-default` and `keycloak-crypto-fips1402` are present, which one wins is arbitrary.
- A deployment intended to run FIPS can silently fall back to non-FIPS BouncyCastle.
- The only trace is a debug-level log line.

The fix should keep failing on ambiguity among the highest-order providers, or at least warn. Only the lower-priority providers (such as the authz-client one) should be dropped silently.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
CryptoProvider first = foundProviders.get(0);
if (foundProviders.size() > 1 && foundProviders.get(1).order() == first.order()) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("Multiple crypto providers with the same order " + first.order()
            + " loaded with the classLoader: " + classLoader + ". Available providers: " + foundProviders);
}
~~~

## 3) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Avoid passing a built string as the format argument to `debugf`

Affected:
- common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:65-69

Explanation:
`logger.debugf(builder.toString())` uses dynamic content as the format string. Any `%` in it would be treated as a format specifier. The message also ends with a trailing `", "`.

Use `debug`, or `debugf` with a real format and the joined names as an argument.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
logger.debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", foundProviders.subList(1, foundProviders.size()).stream()
        .map(p -> p.getClass().getName()).collect(Collectors.joining(", ")));
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Remove the dead encoder calls and validate the input length in `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`

Affected:
- authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:103-121

Explanation:
- Lines 114-115 build two encoders and immediately discard them. They are dead code.
- The method never checks that `signature.length == signLength`. A malformed or truncated JWS signature therefore causes an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` from `System.arraycopy`, instead of an `IOException` that callers can handle as a verification failure.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
if (signature == null || signature.length != signLength) {
    throw new IOException("Invalid signature length");
}
int len = signLength / 2;
// remove the two discarded ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) lines
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Test
Title: Make the test use the right curve per algorithm and verify the re-encoded DER signature

Affected:
- authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:41-57

Explanation:
- A single default `EC` key pair is used for ES256, ES384 and ES512. The default curve is JDK-dependent, so ES384/ES512 are not tested with their real r/s sizes. In particular, the ES512 case with P-521 and its 66-byte components is never exercised.
- The test only checks that the R||S output round-trips through the custom encoder. It never confirms that `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` produces DER the JDK accepts.

Generate the key with the matching curve size and verify the re-encoded signature with `Signature.verify`.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
KeyPairGenerator kpg = KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC");
kpg.initialize(algorithm == ECDSAAlgorithm.ES256 ? 256 : algorithm == ECDSAAlgorithm.ES384 ? 384 : 521);
KeyPair keyPair = kpg.genKeyPair();
...
Signature verifier = Signature.getInstance(JavaAlgorithm.getJavaAlgorithm(algorithm.name()));
verifier.initVerify(keyPair.getPublic());
verifier.update(data);
Assert.assertTrue(verifier.verify(asn1Des));
~~~

## 6) Severity: INFO | Type: Maintainability
Title: Remove the unused hamcrest test dependency

Affected:
- authz/client/pom.xml:67-71

Explanation:
`org.hamcrest:hamcrest` is added with test scope, but the new test only uses `org.junit.Assert`. Remove it unless it is needed.

Proposed fix:
~~~xml
<!-- remove the org.hamcrest:hamcrest dependency block -->
~~~
